methodologyNotes: 13 notable weighted blankets selected as the 2026 buyer comparison set. All 10 brief seeds were verified and kept: Bearaby Napper (Cotton Napper, the beadless chunky-knit category-definer), Gravity Blanket (the original glass-bead DTC blanket that popularized the category), YnM Weighted Blanket (Original Cotton, the Amazon-native budget/best-seller), Baloo Living (all-cotton, no-polyester-liner eco pick), Layla Weighted (dual-sided cooling/warming), Luna Weighted (Cotton, budget value line), Sunday Citizen Snug (the Snug Crystal Weighted Blanket, its actual current weighted-blanket SKU name — 'Snug' alone is a separate non-weighted throw), Quility Premium (Amazon's top-selling budget line, bundled cover), Hush Iced 2.0 (organic-bamboo cooling variant of the Hush Classic), and Brooklinen Weighted Comforter (duvet-style construction vs. a therapy-blanket feel). Three products were added to round the set to 13 and cover comparison axes the seeds leave thin: Silk & Snow Hand-Knitted Weighted Blanket (a second beadless hand-knit competitor to Bearaby, notably cheaper), Luxome Cooling Weighted Blanket (a modular removable-cover system with a bamboo-lyocell cooling option), and Saatva Organic Weighted Blanket (the GOTS-organic-cotton-velvet luxury tier). SOURCING: a hard bot-blocking pattern dominated this research run — gravityblankets.com, balooliving.com, sundaycitizen.co, hushblankets.com, brooklinen.com (own product page), www.silkandsnow.com/en-us, and luxome.com (header-overflow parse error) returned HTTP 429/403 or failed to parse on nearly every direct-fetch attempt across many retries; bearaby.com blocked every attempt outright; lunablanket.com failed DNS resolution entirely from this environment despite resolving fine in search-engine results. ynmhome.com and quilityweightedblanket.com were intermittently reachable (429 on some attempts, 200 on others) and eventually yielded clean official-page fetches; laylasleep.com and saatva.com fetched cleanly on every attempt. For every blocked brand, specs/price were sourced instead from an independently fetched hands-on review (mattressnerd.com, mattressclarity.com, sleepfoundation.org, reviewed.com, nonbiasedreviews.com) or an authorized-retailer/press page (nordstrom.com, refinery29.com, thetismassage.com) — each disclosed per-product in priceNote/provenance. The WebSearch tool's session budget (200 calls) was exhausted partway through this research; all sourcing after that point relied exclusively on WebFetch against URLs already surfaced, which is why a few fields (notably Sunday Citizen's weight-specific pricing and Hush Iced 2.0's per-size weight figures) could not be independently re-confirmed and were left null rather than guessed. priceUsd = the lowest-priced weight/size configuration actually confirmed by a fetched source (not necessarily the brand's absolute cheapest SKU if that specific figure was unreachable); Sunday Citizen's priceUsd is null because sundaycitizen.co blocked every attempt and the one retailer page that loaded (Nordstrom) showed the item sold out with price suppressed, so no fetched source confirmed a current number. IMAGES: Wikimedia Commons was checked first (search for 'weighted blanket' surfaces only generic DIY/homemade-blanket photos and a Hush logo file — no free-licensed photo of any of these 13 specific branded products exists there), so none were used from Commons. Three confirmed manufacturer-CDN studio photos were used, each downloaded and visually inspected to confirm the exact product: Layla (laylasleep.com's own cdn-assets, showing the grey quilted blanket), Saatva (saatva.imgix.net, showing the diamond-quilted velvet throw on a sofa), and YnM (ynmhome.com/cdn/shop/files, a studio shot of the light-grey quilted blanket with a visible 'The Strategist — Best in Class 2025' award badge overlay confirming brand origin). For the remaining 10 products, every located photo was either the review site's own hands-on/testing photography (Bearaby via Sleep Foundation's standardized 'TOP-DOWN' test-photo series and Mattress Nerd's dim-bedroom shot; Baloo and Brooklinen via Reviewed.com's tester posing with the product on a bed; Silk & Snow and Luxome via casual reviewer snapshots) rather than brand press material, or was structurally unreachable (Quility's product images are JS-lazy-loaded SVG placeholders with no resolvable src; Gravity's, Sunday Citizen's, and Hush's own CDN asset paths sit behind the same edge block as their product pages; Luna's domain never resolved) — all omitted rather than mis-labeled as manufacturer photography. accessedAt 2026-08-01 on all entries.

products.name: Bearaby Cotton Napper
products.priceNote: 10 lb (40in x 64in), the lowest-priced/base config, is $199; 15 lb $249, 20 lb $259, 25 lb $279. bearaby.com returned HTTP 429 Too Many Requests on every direct-fetch attempt, so price and specs are sourced from an independently fetched hands-on review.

specs.fill_material: no loose fill — weight comes from the density of a chunky-knit 95% organic cotton / 5% spandex yarn, hand-assembled
specs.cover_material: same knit fabric as the fill (no separate cover) — 95% sustainably farmed organic cotton / 5% spandex, long-staple
specs.cooling_technology: Open chunky-knit construction allows airflow; described as cool-to-touch, but no active cooling material or technology

products.provenance: bearaby.com returned HTTP 429 on every direct-fetch attempt, so specs come from mattressnerd.com's Cotton Napper review, fetched directly (published Jan 6, 2026): confirms a beadless design where weight comes from yarn density (95% organic cotton / 5% spandex, long-staple cotton that resists pilling), an open chunky-knit pattern with no separate cover, four weight/size tiers (10 lb 40x64in $199, 15 lb 40x72in $249, 20 lb 45x72in $259, 25 lb 48x72in $279), full machine-washability (cold water, mild detergent, delicate cycle, low-heat dry), OEKO-TEX and Fairtrade International certification, and cool-to-touch breathability without active cooling tech. A separate general search of bearaby.com's own collection pages corroborates the OEKO-TEX/Fairtrade claim specifically for the grey colorway. No manufacturer image could be confirmed: Sleep Foundation's own standardized 'TOP-DOWN' test-photo (their in-house hands-on testing series, not Bearaby press material) and Mattress Nerd's own dim-bedroom photo were the only located images, both clearly reviewer-shot rather than brand photography, so image is omitted rather than mis-attributed.

Gravity also sells separate Cooling (moisture-wicking cover) and Modernist (100% cotton cover) variants at different prices, not covered here.

specs.fill_material: fine-grade glass beads quilted into a gridded-stitch inner comforter (roughly 4cm-square pockets), with zippers at head/foot and fabric ties along the sides
specs.cover_material: removable polyester micro-fleece / micro-plush duvet cover, zippered

products.provenance: gravityblankets.com returned HTTP 429 on every direct-fetch attempt across the session, so specs come from mattressnerd.com's hands-on review, fetched directly (published Jul 14, 2026): confirms fine-grade glass-bead fill quilted into gridded squares inside a comforter-style insert (zippers at head/foot, ties on the sides), a removable polyester micro-fleece/micro-plush duvet cover, even weight distribution with no bead clumping, a 'temperature neutral' feel (not actively cooling — body heat can build up over extended use) rather than the brand's separate Cooling variant, Single 48x72in / Queen-King 90x90in sizing, 15/20/25 lb Single all priced at $249.99 and 35 lb Queen/King at $299.99, and machine-wash-and-dry for the cover on cold/low heat versus hand-wash-and-air-dry-only for the weighted insert (recorded as machine_washable: false since the insert itself cannot go in a machine). No OEKO-TEX or other certification is mentioned. No manufacturer image could be confirmed: gravityblankets.com's own CDN sits behind the same block as its product pages, and mattressnerd.com's own review photos are reviewer test shots (not brand press material), so image is omitted.

Ten weight options exist from 5 lb (Toddler) up to 30 lb (King); per-tier price breakdown beyond the page's headline $79 could not be independently confirmed.

specs.fill_material: glass beads encased in breathable polyester fabric compartments, sewn into 4.7in x 4.7in quilted pockets
specs.cooling_technology: Moisture-wicking fibers and a finer cotton weave for airflow; no active cooling material on this cotton SKU (a separate 100% Bamboo Viscose line offers stronger cooling)

products.provenance: ynmhome.com's product page (reachable on a subset of attempts; blocked with HTTP 429 on others) fetched directly: confirms Contour Technology fill engineering, glass-bead fill in 4.7x4.7in cotton-fabric pockets, natural breathability via moisture-wicking fibers and finer weave, duvet-cover-compatible corner loops, a 1-year warranty, ten weight options from 5 to 30 lb across Kids Toddler (36x48in) through King (80x87in) sizing, and a headline price of $79.00. mattressclarity.com's independent review of YNM's 100% Bamboo Viscose sibling product, fetched directly, corroborates the shared brand construction (glass microbeads in ~2x2in sewn-through squares, corner/side duvet loops, machine-washable with a caution that blankets over 12-15 lb may need a commercial laundromat machine) and separately observed the same flat $79 price point recurring across that line's own weight tiers. Image fetched directly from ynmhome.com's own Shopify CDN path and visually confirmed: a folded light-grey quilted blanket with a 'The Strategist — New York, Best in Class 2025' award badge overlaid, confirming brand-official marketing photography.

specs.fill_material: lead-free mini glass beads sewn into three differently sized pockets for contouring, with cotton batting (no polyester liner)
specs.cover_material: 100% cotton shell throughout, inside and out

products.provenance: balooliving.com returned HTTP 429 on every direct-fetch attempt, so specs come from reviewed.com's hands-on review, fetched directly: confirms an all-cotton shell filled with lead-free mini glass beads sewn into three graduated pocket sizes for even contouring, zero polyester lining or filling (unlike competitors, per the brand's own claim), machine-washable on a home washing machine (gentle cycle, cold water, tumble dry low), an optional purchasable linen cover, sizing from Mini (40x60in) through the tested Throw (42x60in, listed elsewhere at 42x72in — reviewed.com's own measured figure of 42x60in is used here) up to King (80x87in), a 9-25 lb weight range, catalog pricing of $149-$219, and the specific tested 12 lb Throw at $159-$198. No manufacturer image could be confirmed: the only located photos, from reviewed.com's own photoshoot, show the tester posing with the blanket on a bed (clearly the review site's own photography, including a close-up of the brand tag) rather than Baloo press material, so image is omitted.
